utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, it's now for you to cross-examine the witness if you wish to. Since this is the first witness and since you're representing yourself, you should be told about the purpose and limitations of cross-examination. The purpose of cross-examination is to ask questions, to test the witness's evidence and credibility, that is, whether he or she should be believed or not. According to the Tribunal's Rules, it is limited to the subject matter of the evidence in chief, that is the evidence given in answer to questions from the Prosecution and to questions as to credibility. It is also the opportunity to ask questions relating to your case, that is the case which you wish to put forward in your defence. The Trial Chamber may permit questions on other matters. Cross-examination is subject to the control of the Trial Chamber in order to make it effective for the ascertainment of the truth and avoid the needless consumption of time. It is restricted to matters relevant to the issues in the trial and must not be used as a way of harassing or intimidating witnesses. Any questions which may reveal the identity of protected witnesses must be asked in closed session. This statement will be put into writing and given to the accused. Now, Mr. Milosevic, do you have any questions for the witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] As far as I was able to understand, Mr. Bakalli is a protected witness.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let me see. We've had that translated. He's not a protected witness; he's Mr. Bakalli. So you can ask anything about his identity if you wish.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I read in the papers that he was a protected witness. And then they published that it was -- they were referring to Bakalli, speaking of that protected witness, but thank you for the information you've just given me. If you ensure that the witness gives me yes and no answers, then I shall be, of course, brief.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: Cross-examined by Mr. Milosevic:

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You said, Mr. Bakalli, that Kosovo private parallel schools were set up because of apartheid. Yes or no? Could you give me a yes or no answer, please?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they weren't private, but they were public schools. They were not state schools of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And to which state did those schools belong?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There were elementary schools, secondary schools, university. They were all under the Serbian Ministry of Education, financed from Serbia, with Serb curricula which you organised.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm speaking about the parallel schools. You said -- you mentioned parallel private schools because of apartheid. You mentioned that you organised parallel schools because of apartheid. Now, I would like your answer, yes or no, please. Did you or didn't you?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, except we didn't call them private schools, and they were not private schools. They were public schools, where the people collected money, the population, as far as they could.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, just keep the answers as short as you can.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said you were a professor of sociology at the university in Pristina?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you consider that every student of sociology, each one of your students, should be able to explain what apartheid is?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you explain to us what apartheid means? What is apartheid?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Apartheid with yes or no, or do you want the opinion of a professor?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: A short --

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you to explain to us what apartheid is.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: A short explanation, Mr. Bakalli, please.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Okay. If collectivity, a group, a national group or a racial group, is put by the state into a position outside of the government, outside of the economy, thrown out of education and cultural affairs, that is apartheid.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The school curriculum for Kosovo, was it different from the school curriculum for children all over Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just give us an example.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For example, history of the Albanian people, which was foreseen under the autonomy system, was eliminated under the Serbian curricula later, and there are other examples of this.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't think you understand me. Obviously you haven't. I didn't ask you what the curriculum and programme was in your private schools. What I'm asking you is about the programme, the curriculum, of state schools throughout the territory of Serbia, which was the same for all schools and all children in Serbia. It was a universal curriculum. Now, according to that state Serb curriculum, was the programme different for Albanian children? According to the Serb curriculum for state schools throughout the territory, did Albanian children have a different programme, different from all the other children in Serbia? That's what I'm asking.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, there was no difference, or difference in the curricula for Albanian language education. It was a unified programme for all of Serbia, for the Albanians and for the Serbs in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that all children in Serbia followed the same school programme, the same curriculum?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In state schools for the Albanian children, was tuition in the Albanian language?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It could have been, but they did not accept such schools, to go to such schools, because you imposed the curricula. You people imposed the leaders, the principals of the schools, and the heads of the faculties.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a moment, please. A moment ago you agreed with me that the school programme, the curriculum, was the same for all the children of Serbia, in Serbia, and now you -- I'm asking you whether, for the Albanian children, tuition is Albanian, and you said yes, it was, for those who went to state schools, but that they didn't want to go to state schools because we imposed a programme on them. Now, I claim that for all Albanian children, tuition was in the Albanian language. Is that correct or is it not? I'm talking about state schools.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not in Albanian, or there were not Albanian schools in Albanian language in Kosovo, because the education system was radically changed and the Albanian population refused to take part in it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you claim that the Albanian children didn't go to state schools at all?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I would say that almost no one went to them. Perhaps there were a few minor exceptions. I don't know of any students who did go to such schools.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How many exceptions were there, Albanians who went to state schools? Give us an example. Roughly how many Albanians going to state schools?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't really think there were any exceptions, but it could be that there were. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, you say you don't know how many of them there were. Was tuition in Albanian for them, for those?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know. I don't really know of any student or pupil who went to the school, into that school system, once it was put under apartheid.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So what you're saying is the following: You're saying something that in fact you now say you don't know.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that I knew that Albanians had taken part in the Serbian educational system. What I don't know is if there were Albanians taking part in your education system. That I don't know. I don't think so, but I am not sure. There could have been.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you say "our" education system? You used the word "our." Did you consider that the Albanians were citizens of Serbia or not?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: From the moment that the parliament of Kosova approved the Constitution of Kosova, they did not feel themselves that they were any longer citizens of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll come to that later, but a moment ago you used the word "apartheid" again. I should suggest that you read the United Nations definition of "apartheid" before you do so again. What about the Hungarian children? Did the Hungarian children follow the same curriculum as all the other children in Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That had been regulated earlier with school curricula under the autonomy status in Vojvodina. This was also for the Hungarian students. What happened later, once you came to power, I don't know what happened to the Hungarians in the Vojvodina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yourself that you were an intellectual who always wrote since 1981 to the present day, and you say you don't know what was going on in your own country. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You don't have the right, because I have observed events, but I can't tell you in detail of what happened to school curricula, the school curricula of the Albanian state who -- of the Serb state. I can't tell you if the Hungarians in the Vojvodina accepted them or not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We have taken note of the fact that throughout Serbia all the children had the same school programme, the same curriculum. And then I went on to ask you, because you say you don't know how many Albanian children attended tuition in the Albanian language, I asked you whether you know whether the Hungarian children had tuition in Hungarian, the Bulgarian children in Bulgarian, and so on and so forth. Do you know anything about that either? You don't seem to. You don't know that either. Just say yes or no. You don't have to go into any lengthy explanations. You don't know, I see.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know whether in Serbia the members of the Bulgarian minority attended tuition in Bulgarian. You don't know that either?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you consider that the school programme which was in force for all children in Serbia should not be enforced for Albanian children?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's good for school programmes to be universal for everyone but with concrete, specific elements, in particular, for national elements, for national specific elements. And from the year 1974 onwards, we had school curricula which were approved by the parliament of Kosova, and they had no relations -- Serbia had no right of interference under the Constitution in such school curricula.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As we are not challenging the fact that national minorities in Serbia and national -- that national minorities in Serbia are able to attend tuition in their own languages, and as the Albanian children were taught and had tuition in Albanian and were taught the Albanian literature and all other subjects were taught in the Albanian language, do you consider that there is a special Albanian mathematics, physics, biology, chemistry, without going into the exact natural sciences. Philosophy, for example. Was there a separate Albanian Plato, Aristotle, John Moore or anybody like that? Giordano Bruno, perhaps? Galileo Galilei, and so on and so forth? In your opinion, apart from the element of language - and the language element was guaranteed to one and all - why would you think that the school curriculum for Albanian children should be different than for all the other children in Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not only for Albanian children but for the children of all the nationalities of Yugoslavia. Which -- with the exception of mathematics. Giordano Bruno, of course, was common to all the nationalities, but each one did have its own curricula. Not for natural sciences but for history and for culture and for language.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, I don't suppose you're challenging as far as culture and language is concerned and overall tuition that every national minority was able to be taught in their own language in all state schools. Was the Albanian language -- was Albanian the official language in Kosovo up until this war?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, on the basis of the Constitution of 1974.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you say that it wasn't on the basis of the change in the Constitution, that it wasn't an official language. Is that what you're saying? You are under a solemn declaration here, Mr. Bakalli.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You needn't remind me of that. The language of the administration under Milosevic was -- you could use Albanian for some documents.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For what documents couldn't the Albanian language be used?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry. That is a subject for which I'm not an expert, legal questions. I am not in a position to reply to that, Your Honours.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. If an Albanian is taken to court, was it considered that he could address the court only in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. Many of the prisoners whom you took under your reign could -- formally were given the right to reply in Albanian, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What do you mean when you say "formally"? Does it mean that that right was not accorded to them on a regular basis; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They were not banned from using their language in court. The question is rather: Why were they in court?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: For the moment, the question is: What language were they allowed to use? And the answer is: They were allowed to use Albanian. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that the Serbian government didn't want to implement the agreement on the education system.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The three-plus-three-plus-three group, is that something that is known to you? I'm talking about the group on behalf of the government of Serbia was led by Minister Vlatomir Vico; on behalf of the Albanian side, it was Professor Fehmi Agani; and on behalf of Centar Ucidi, it was Dom Vicenzo Pajla. Do you know about this group? Have you heard about it? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know about it because I've worked for it. I brought the documents which you yourself signed. But I did not work in it precisely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke about the subject, and therefore, I assume that if you talk about a subject, you know something about that subject. You said that no results were achieved. You said that nothing had been done, nothing implemented.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember -- do you remember - and give me a yes or no answer, please - that up until September, the month of September that year, the Albanian side took over the technical faculty, 20.000 square metres in all, and the faculty of economics and faculty of law, which amounted to 16.000 square metres? Do you remember that; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. A process began, sort of, but it was sabotaged, and there was no success. It was never realised under the -- according to the document.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: How do you consider that it was sabotaged if the Albanian side, in material terms, took over the buildings, which amounted to 20.000 square metres, 16.000 square metres? How, then, do you say that this was sabotage? It took possession of those buildings in order to organise its tuition at the faculties, at the university. Do you consider that to be sabotage; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm convinced, yes, that from what I heard from Fehmi Agani, and Fehmi Agani told you at that meeting, in May, that they were totally unsatisfied with the reaction of the Serbian side and with the contacts between the Albanian and Serbian sides, under the aegis of San Edjidio.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Leave aside May and everything you've just said about that meeting. Let's leave that aside for the moment. We'll go into that later on. What I'm asking you now is the following: In your opinion, is it possible to describe a sabotage, the implementation of a programme, when the material fact is that at the university, they took over buildings which were 20.000 square metres large and 16.000 square metres large; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that was a realisation or implementation of any kind. I don't think that was the realisation of the agreement.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: For our listeners, let me add that this was the peak, the top. As for secondary and primary schools, everything had already been solved; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This did not apply to the elementary or the high school all the time. They have worked in the cellars in private homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You claim, therefore, that the Albanians did not go to primary and secondary schools, state ones?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you said that the only possibility for schooling Albanians was the parallel system of schools?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, that's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were the rights of Albanian children to attend classes in Albanian language denied to them?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because they were denied of having their own programme.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is the body that approves the curriculum in any country?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In our country, it was the Minister of Education, to all children in Serbia. Thus, in Kosova, we had the Pedagogical Council of Kosova, as a body of the parliament of Kosova, under the Constitution of 1974.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: We'll get to that Constitution later on. My question referred to whether somebody denied the right to Albanian children to attend classes in Albanian. Please reply with yes or no.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are claiming that Albanian children were not able to attend classes in Albanian?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Only under the illegal system, only in the cellars. In the state schools, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are claiming that in state schools, Albanian children did not attend classes in Albanian language. In state schools, Albanian children could not attend classes in Albanian language; is that what you're claiming? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness replied: "Excellent."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said yesterday that my speech in Gazimestan directly led to changes in the Constitution; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not exactly so. I said that after that, we had the amendments to the Constitution, but your speech in Gazimestan was a speech, in my view, that was a programme of war.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. We'll, let's leave that aside for the time being. So you said, and then you repeated again today, that after my speech in Gazimestan, the Constitution was changed. All right. Do you remember the date of the Kosovo battle? Do you know that that took place on the 28th of June, 1389?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that 600 years was celebrated on the same day in 1989, on the 20th of June?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Is it true that the Serbian Assembly proclaimed changes or amendments to the Constitution on the 28th of March, 1989, which means three months prior to the speech to which you ascribe the fact that it led to changes in the Constitution? You just said a moment ago that after my speech, there were changes in the Constitution, and now I'm giving you the dates that were actually formally recorded as being the 28th of March, 1989. This is three months before the date after which you claim the Constitution had been changed. So what is going on here, Mr. Bakalli?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let the witness answer. Yes, the point is made that the changes were three months before the speech. Now, Mr. Bakalli, what's your answer to that?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The initiative was taken earlier, but it does not relate to what I'm saying. Yesterday I did not at all say that his address -- that they immediately led to the constitutional changes. I referred to it before Your Honours because I thought that it was kind of a call for war, a programme for war, and the initiative, the legal initiative to make the constitutional amendment was taken a couple of months ago. But, as I said yesterday, the Constitution was changed in an unlawful way through use of force. I do not relate his speech to the changes of the Constitution, as something that happened right away, as he's claiming.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, just a while ago, two minutes ago, you said that the changes in the Constitution took place after my speech in Gazimestan. Yes or no, please. At any rate, everyone was able to hear that.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that the essence of the constitutional changes is related to your speech in Gazimestan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even after that?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After your speech, the changes occurred.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Could you please quote what you're saying from my speech?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What really impressed me, but I don't have the document with me here, what I -- it really impressed me at that time was the -- your way of addressing it more or less, so that we in Yugoslavia today are waging a political struggle, a struggle waged may assume proportions of an armed war. All what I got from your speech in Gazimestan was the impression that you unfurled a programme of military action or crisis in Yugoslavia. This is what I had the impression then. This is what I wrote about, and this is what I'm telling this Honourable Court today.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Okay. I didn't say what you just said, but you did say what we heard from the Prosecution, and this is something that I disputed here when I gave my opening speech. Are you able to provide to me what you wrote at the time? I would be able to give you my speech and newspapers from 1989 containing my speech. Are you able to give me the other papers? You indicated here time, struggle, and you indicated here newspapers Vreme and some other of our newspapers. So would you be able to show me these articles of yours that were published in these papers?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, because at that moment I did not write in Nasa Borba and Vreme, but I did write in Albanian-language papers, in a letter I sent to Eagleburger which I published in Vjesnik in Zagreb and in Albanian paper in Pristina. But I don't have them with me now so that I can cite them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. But you would be able to provide that for us in Albanian, in Serbian, in Croatian, the articles that were published in the Vjesnik paper. So you would be able to do that? Yes or no? And we would be able to see from those papers how you explained that I in fact issued a call for war in Gazimestan. Is this what you're claiming, that this is what it says in your text?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I've written there that there you made public a militant -- unfurled, I'm saying, a militant programme. I didn't say you declared war but that you have unfurled, as I'm saying, a militant, a military programme, militant programme.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said what you've said. Everything's been recorded in the transcript, so we'll be able to compare and see whether what you said here was in fact printed somewhere or you lied under oath. But let's leave that aside for the time being. Is it true -- is it true that the Assembly of the Autonomous Province of Kosovo -- I apologise. Let me ask you something else that has to do with what you mentioned. When I said the 28th of March, you said, "Well, yes, some initiatives were launched." On the 28th of March, initiatives were not launched. On the 28th of March, there was a final act that took place. So on the 28th of March, 1989, there was a final proclamation of the Constitution at the session of the Serbian Assembly. So there were no initiatives. That had started much earlier. A final act took place on the 28th of March.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, we must move on to a question. What's the question?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: On the 28th of March, which is in fact three months prior to the 28th of June, that was the day when the final act of proclamation of the Constitution of Serbia took place. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know remember the dates exactly. I cannot pronounce my views on that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reply is very important, because yesterday you said, and then once again repeated here, that the changes took place after the speech in Gazimestan.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I think we've dealt with this point. You've made your point. The witness says he doesn't remember the date. We've got the evidence, and we'll have to consider it in due course. If you'd like to move on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the Assembly of Kosovo accepted constitutional changes prior to the 28th of March? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say no. This is the argument, please, that the parliament of Kosovo was surrounded by police and tanks. I have personal information --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't let us continue this argument. We've continued long enough on the 28th of March. Let's move on to another topic, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This is not the same topic, Judge May, because there are some other issues that are linked to this which are very important. As we're talking about the Constitution --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's have another question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the Assembly of Serbia, pursuant to the Constitution then in force, would be unable to implement these changes without a previous approval of the Kosovo Assembly? Thank you. Now, did the Kosovo Assembly approve this decision on adopting the constitutional amendments? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not a matter of saying yes or no. I can say yes, but it was under the pressure of tanks which were outside the parliament building.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ...

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You were the only one who saw those tanks. What I'm asking you is this: Did the Constitution -- did the Assembly pass this decision on adopting constitutional amendments? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, with force, use of force.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that at the session of the Kosovo Assembly only 14 deputies voted against this proposal?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Some were braver and said, "Irrespective of violence, I don't agree with the changes."

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What I asked is whether it is true that only 14 deputies in the Kosovo Assembly voted against this proposal. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Please try to focus on the answer. Is it true that a member of the Constitutional Commission of Serbia was from Kosovo, and his name was Professor Surija Popovci. He was also an Albanian, which perhaps is not immediately obvious to everybody here. Is it true that a member of the Constitutional Commission of Serbia was an Albanian and was from Kosovo? Is it true that Professor Popovci appeared on television prior to the session of the Assembly and supported the amendments?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but, please ask me a question why he appeared on television. Please ask me.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters are kindly asking the speakers to pause between question and answer. Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The interpreters have a request, first of all, that there should be a pause, both of you, between question and answer, so could you keep that in mind. Yes. Mr. Bakalli, after you've been cross-examined, the Prosecution will have a chance to re-examine you, which means that if there are any matters, relevant matters, which they want to ask about or you want to give explanations about, you can do it then. Meanwhile, just concentrate, if you would, on answering the questions. Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Sinan Hasani is?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At the time constitutional changes were implemented, was Sinan Hasani President of the Presidency of Yugoslavia?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. He was Chairman of the Presidency of Yugoslavia, and he was on our side.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sinan Hasani is an Albanian, and he was President of the Presidency of Yugoslavia. He attended the session of the Serbian Assembly during which the Constitution was promulgated on the 28th of March. Is that true?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that also all other high officials on the federal and republic level of Albanian nationality were present as well? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. Sinan, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you claiming that only Sinan Hasani was present from the Albanian side?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Probably there has been someone else. I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: At that time, who held the position of the Chairman of the Province Party Board at the time? Was that position held by an Albanian or a Serb?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: An Albanian whom you have appointed. You brought him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: My question was: Was that person an Albanian or a Serb?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: An Albanian.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were other Albanians who were present there, did they come because I appointed them?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Gentlemen, please. When you deprive a society of its constitutional position, don't believe that they are happy to come to a meeting when you have deprived them, stripped them of their constitutional rights. Hasani was there, but you have to ask him why he was there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who appointed Sinan Hasani to the Presidency of the -- of Yugoslavia, to be the President of the Presidency?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: To say it bluntly, you, because Albania was under the influence and tutelage of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Sinan Hasani was elected by the Kosovo Assembly as a member of the Yugoslav Presidency much prior to that. Why don't you carefully consider this? Perhaps you made a mistake.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, no. I'm not wrong. You are wrong. Sinan Hasani came to the Presidency of Yugoslavia after you were elected Chairman of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you claim that I was the one who appointed Sinan Hasani to the Presidency of Yugoslavia. Is that what you're claiming? Yes or no, please?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Excellent.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness replied: "You're welcome."

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Did any of the Albanian deputies who had attended the session of the Serbian Assembly which promulgated the Constitution dispute this Constitution? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't -- you mean in the Serb parliament?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was not a Serb Assembly. It was an Assembly of the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know who Muharrem Ismaili is?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is he a friend of yours and also a director of a bank in Kosovo, also an Albanian?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: He's a Kosovar Albanian. He was the director of Kosova Bank. He is no longer there. And he's a friend of mine. I don't know why you're asking me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Because I want to put another question to you. Did you ask him to come and talk to me?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Never. That's not true. I have never talked with him that I wanted to talk with you. Never. I've never done that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying that you did not ask, through Muharrem Ismaili, to come and see me?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say in my full responsibility, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you told us how the local security chief, Gajic, under inverted commas, told you about the "Scorched Earth Plan," the so-called "Scorched Earth Plan." Wasn't it logical for you to bring up this issue while talking to me; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I could have done that, but I did not. I didn't want to become -- to convey the views of others. Maybe I should have done that. I should have done that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. This is enough material for us to give us an idea of how seriously you assessed this matter. You told us yourself that you were involved in scheduling a meeting with -- headed by Mr. Rugova in order to find a political solution; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You also said that the delegation of the Serbian government, headed by Deputy Prime Minister Ratko Markovic, came only once and held only one meeting with your representatives in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that two meetings between the Serbian delegation and the Albanian side produced joint communiques and that there are joint communiques from two meetings, whereas you said that there wasn't a communique from that single meeting? So is it true that there were, in fact, two meetings; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We had only one meeting between the two delegations, and we issued two separate communiques. We didn't have two meetings.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that the delegation of the government of Serbia, headed by the deputy prime minister, Professor Ratko Markovic, came to Pristina 11 times to attend previously scheduled meetings which were not attended by the Albanian representatives. We were able to see this on television every time, Mr. Bakalli. You don't need to be specifically informed of this. Is it true that this delegation went to Pristina 11 times and the Albanian side failed to show up? Mr. Bakalli, yesterday --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, let him answer.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may be that the delegation headed by Professor Markovic has come. We have often seen delegations from Serbia coming to Pristina. I went to receive the Albanian side, but these meetings were the result of an arrogance dictated by them as being the HOS.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let's try and get to the bottom of it. What's being put is that there was not simply one meeting, but there were occasions at which the Serbian delegation came to Kosovo to meet, but the Albanian representatives, as I understand it, didn't come. Now, is that the case or not?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but these meetings were not planned beforehand. Yes, there are some cases.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were 11 such cases; yes or no, Mr. Bakalli?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have not kept track of them. I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that they were not scheduled; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you know that these cases, of whose existence you are not aware, were not scheduled previously?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. As I said, they were unscheduled before, as such, to conduct genuine negotiations.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When asked by the Prosecutor yesterday, you replied that there was no will to conduct negotiations on the Serbian side. This is the reply you gave. You can check this. You, in fact, said that the Serbian side was not willing to discuss political settlement. And now here, we can see that they, in fact, travelled to Pristina 11 times and, in fact, your side was not willing to negotiate; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true. It is not true that the Serb side was particularly interested in discussing the status and political issues related to Kosovo position. It was the Albanian side that was interested in such issues. Your delegations came more to deliver lectures against terrorism, to calm down the situation, to calm down the citizens so that it would be easier for you to rule over us, but not to resolve the question of the status of Kosova under the expression of the will of the Albanian people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's leave aside the expressions you used, such as the expression of "the will of the Albanian people." That's not what I asked you. What I asked you was: Is it true that the delegation, after a meeting between me and Rugova, at which you yourself were present, came to Pristina 11 times to continue those negotiations and that communiques were issued from only two meetings, whereas the other attempts were blocked by you and that you now claim that it was the Serbian side which came to Pristina on 11 occasions, did not have the goodwill to negotiate? Is that what you're saying; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is not true. Mr. Milosevic, you have confused, I think -- you are confusing some issues. After the first and last meeting between the two delegations - and I was a member of the Albanian delegation - we did not receive any offer or did not have any other meetings as such.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You therefore claim that what I have just asked you, and whether -- I asked you whether that is correct or not. Your answer is that it is not correct. Am I reading you correctly? Is it correct that the federal premier, an American otherwise - his name is Milan Panic - sometime in 1993, together with Vance and Owen, went to Kosovo and that then too nobody wished to talk to them?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, no, because the prime minister of Yugoslavia did meet with Ibrahim Rugova, if you remember. They were taken in a picture with both hands up. But I don't think it has much bearing to this issue we are discussing.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: It doesn't matter about that. The answer is you don't know; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't remember.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, you were an advisor to Demaci; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, for a couple of months before the beginning of the conference of Rambouillet.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. So you were an advisor of Adem Demaci and you have just confirmed that. Now, as far as I remember - and this is my next question - as far as I remember, you said yesterday that you had nothing to do with the KLA. Now, if I'm not remembering this correctly, or perhaps I didn't hear it correctly, I'm asking you now: Did you have any connections with the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the troops of the National Liberation Army of Kosova and with the staff, the General Staff, I had no connections. As I said, I did have contacts as an advisor - orientations, political and diplomatic advice for the KLA, which was coming up publicly and legally - and in Pristina, contacts with Demaci, a few months, two or three months before the Rambouillet conference. And there was a disagreement between me and Mr. Demaci, so I insisted that the KLA take part in the conference at Rambouillet, irrespective of the initial policies and platforms of the Rambouillet conference. They didn't take into consideration all the aspirations of the Albanian people, but Rambouillet was an important international factor for solving the Kosovo issue in a peaceful and political manner, and at the same time, it helped to affirm the international presence of the KLA. So I insisted that the KLA take part in the Rambouillet conference.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As you have finished with giving us an explanation which I didn't ask you for, I have to go back to my question. You confirmed a moment ago that you were an advisor to Demaci, and you also confirmed a moment ago that you had nothing to do with the KLA.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: With the troops, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday your answer was that you had nothing to do with the KLA, and it is common knowledge that Demaci is the head of the political wing of the KLA. You are now trying to bypass the truth, if I can put it that way, because you say you had no contacts with the troops. I didn't ask you about which soldier or terrorist you contacted with. My question was: Did you have any connection or links with the KLA? Adem Demaci was the head of the political wing of the KLA and you were his advisor; is that correct?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'd like to alter my answer slightly. I had contacts with the KLA, in the form of suggestions, advice, political advice. But I don't want to hide anything; in fact, I'm proud of this.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I did not ask you whether you shot or placed bombs or anything else. I just asked you whether you had any connections with the KLA.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment. Mr. Milosevic, he's given an explanation of what he says his connection with the KLA was, so we've heard that. Now, can we go on to the next point?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we can, we can.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, you are a deputy in the Assembly of Kosovo, and you are in the Alliance for the Future of Kosovo; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yesterday you said that you were an independent intellectual, a deputy, and not that you were a deputy of the Alliance for the Future of Kosovo; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You changed the question and asked me now I should say yes or no. Just give me a moment to explain. I was a deputy on the list of the Alliance for the Future of Kosovo, because the elections took place on a proportional system and the parties have closed lists. I was asked, as an independent intellectual, to put my name on their list, and I still -- but I still remain independent as such. I like the alliance, I like the people who are in it, so I accepted to have my name put on the list. They called me, and so I did it. As such, I am an independent deputy in the parliament of Kosova, from the list of the alliance, and am a member of the parliamentary group of the Alliance for the Future of Kosova. I don't see what is contradictory here. But I am not a member of any party and I have never been a member, and today I am not a member of the Alliance Party.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are a deputy of the alliance. That is what you have confirmed yourself and that is common knowledge. Everybody knows that who knows what parliamentary elections are. You are on their list, a deputy on their list, a deputy of the alliance; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I'm on the list of the alliance.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the president of the Alliance for the Future of Kosovo Ramus Aradinai?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you an advisor of Ramus Aradinai now, at present?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Should he need my advice, I give it to him.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know, in connection with your president, the president of the alliance, that as he wrote, as Elefteros Tipos wrote, according to reports of the British service, where he is called the Mafia Ramus, that Aradinai, is head of the Albanian underground and he engages in trafficking and dirty work in the Balkans and the whole of Europe? Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I do not know that, and that is exactly the opposite of my opinion. I have a very high consideration of Ramus Aradinai.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All I'm asking you is whether you know what Elefteros wrote about him, and I quoted what he said. It is a newspaper.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: What is Elefteros Tipos anyway?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that there is a Mafia in Djakovica for smuggling tobacco, armaments, and this is Ramus Aradinai who is in charge of that, your President? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't know that. I know that he was a good -- he's a good person. He was a very good commander. He was a very skilful commander, and is a good, young politician.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: 1986, he did his military service in the JNA, the Yugoslav People's Army, and after that, for a number of years, he was in the French Foreign Legion. Do you know that?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The one I know and the other I didn't know. I have never asked him, so he never told me.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that he was the organiser of armed activities by Albanian terrorists in Macedonia and in Southern Serbia in recent months? Do you know about that?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. On the contrary. But I know on the contrary, from conversations, that we had to exert our influence in the Presevo Valley and Macedonia to calm the situation and get rid of the violence there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Aradinai is accused of having committed the murders of a number of Albanians and Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. And I don't think that there could ever be any possible evidence for such accusations. I haven't heard of any anyway.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it true that Aradinai was wounded when he threw bombs at a house, the house of a Sadik Musai, a fellow Albanian from the party?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The information you're bringing here you've got -- you were very badly informed. I would ask you to be more careful with the information you present.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Don't spend any more time. Now, Mr. Milosevic, I think we're getting some way from the detail of this witness's evidence. We've had the questions which you've put in relation to his credibility. So if you can move to another topic.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You spoke of the killing of Jashari yesterday in Donja Prekaz. Do you know that the police surrounded the house to arrest them and that they did not want to surrender themselves to the police and that they shot at the policeman?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's your -- what you're saying. I don't know any details.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that the police gave them two hours to surrender. So you know the details. Did you say yesterday that the police gave them a two-hour time span to surrender when they surrounded them?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: No. What he said was -- just a moment. Just a moment. What he said was that you, Mr. Milosevic, said that to him. That was his evidence yesterday, that you said it to him.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That I told him that they had two hours to surrender.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that Jashari -- let me say before that, do you know that for those two hours -- during those two hours it was the women and children that came out of the house mostly?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, but I know that women and children were murdered in the house and around the house.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The ones that came out of the house certainly weren't killed, but do you know that Jashari killed even his own uncle at the time because his uncle wanted to go out and surrender? I don't know whether it was his mother's or his father's brother, but an uncle any way. The uncle wanted to go out and surrender, but Jashari shot him. This is contained in the court reports pertaining to the investigation of the event that took place.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know, and I don't believe it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you consider that a two-hour time period is insufficient for terrorists to decide whether they're going to give themselves up or not and that once those two hours had expired they once again opened fire at the policemen and that those who thought -- who wanted to leave the house left? Do you consider that any other police force anywhere in the world would have fled when somebody was shooting at it from a barricaded house behind whose walls there were killers? Is that you're opinion?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have nothing to do with police operations, so I can't answer your question. But what I know is that you killed civilians, children. Twelve -- twelve thousand civilians, including old people, women, children, pregnant women, saying all the time that you were fighting terrorism. That I know. And in the case of the Jasharis, after them you killed -- around them you killed women and children.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about the experience the police force had in that same place, Donji Prekaz, on the 13th of May, 1981, when in following barricaded criminals four policemen lost their lives, and the fifth policeman died later on, succumbing to his serious wounds? Because ethnicity is essential. There were three Serbs and one Muslim and one Albanian. They were policemen who were killed in the conflict with those criminals. I assume that you think that five policemen should have been killed once again by Jashari whom, as you know, killed Serbs and Albanians in order to loot them and pilfer them. He killed them for money. He wasn't very -- he didn't mind killing an Albanian or slitting his throat if an Albanian happened to have some money on him.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... question.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone, please. Could the speaker switch on his microphone, please? Microphone, please.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The interpreters did not hear the question. The microphone was off.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, I think we've dealt fully with this, and you've given your evidence.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May I continue?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: [No translation]

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're not getting any interpretation.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that people were put into prison for political reasons in my day, but nobody could have been imprisoned --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Go on.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: -- for political reasons. Let me repeat the question. You said that yesterday in my day there were people who were put in prison, arrested, for political reasons, and I say that nobody was allowed to be imprisoned for political reasons and arrested. If what you said is true, if what you said is true, that in prison there was an Albanian, for political reasons, an Albanian had been put in prison for political reasons, did you do anything about it, and did you raise the issue in any of the Western embassies where you said you went to attend receptions? Did you raise that question and issue with Amnesty International, perhaps, or Helsinki Watch or the Yugoslav authorities? How come you did nothing about it? You did not raise this issue because you know that if you had to it would have at least become public knowledge that there was a man, some poor sufferer, who had been arrested by the authorities. Did you raise those issues at all?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I raised them in -- to the organs of civil rights in Serbia and all the states in Europe and America, the organs of the United Nations too. Everywhere we said, we told them that you are imprisoning people for political reasons. And as a total, you were keeping 2.000 Albanians in prisons for -- imprisoned for political reasons. You know how they were taken, how they were imprisoned. In Djakove, for instance, they just took people out of their houses, in the streets, and sole -- and sent them off to prison in Serbia. There was even -- there was some sort of formal sentence that was passed on them without a normal legal procedure being carried out, and they were sentenced to Draconic sentences and were taken off to prison. I know that I'd like to make another accusation here.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what were the sentences? How long were the sentences?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Let us wait for the next question. Yes. The next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Apart from that propaganda about the so-called arrest of people, did you ever state the names of the people who had been arrested allegedly? Yes or no? Who did you give the names to of those arrested people, people who were arrested for political reasons?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Please, Honoured Court, you should be aware that there are many humanitarian societies, even in Serbia, who know the names better than I do. Pressure was exerted against them from the state. They themselves wanted the prisoners to be liberated, the Albanian prisoners who were in Serb prisons. I'm not talking about normal prisoners, normal convicts. I'm talking about political prisoners under the reign of Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You were asked who you gave the names -- you were asked who you gave the names to.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: There are two or three Serb councils there -- which are maintaining a very positive attitude. Mrs. Biznarko knows. Another distinguished lady - I don't remember the name now - knows about them. Then all -- all the international institutions engaged in human rights protection know them, as well as the Kosova Council for the Protection of Human Rights and Freedoms. They all know the exact names, and they have sent these names to the relevant bodies, whereas the prosecutors, many prosecutors, always go to the Minister of Justice of Serbia and present him the names. So the Serbian authorities know. They know whom am I talking about, who the political prisoners are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you for the names of the victims, the alleged victims that you are speaking about and not the name of the lady, as you say, that you contacted. Do you have the names of those victims?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: We have the names of the political prisoners as well as the victims. For the moment, I don't have them with me. I might tell that -- I might tell you only that I remember -- I told you the name of Ukshin Hoti, the way he was taken out of prison and disappeared without leaving any trace. Then I -- many other names I may give you at any other moment as pieces of the evidence or through witnesses to The Hague Tribunal.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, to clarify things, you say that there were political prisoners who were condemned for political reasons, for verbal offences. Do you know that we have abolished verbal offence as such from the Criminal Code?

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: The witness said, "Yes," earlier.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, but they changed it later. For example, the accusations made against a large number of youths who are sent to prison was that you have invited NATO to come here and that you are the rear front of KLA. They didn't have any arms, any uniforms on them. They were taken to prison right from the street or from the homes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You're talking about the KLA terrorists who were arrested? Is that who you're talking about?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I'm not talking about them. I'm talking about ordinary citizens who were taken away from their homes in Djakove, for example. They did not have anything to do with KLA. But you accused them in order to fill the Serbian prisons with them. And I think that those 2.000 people who are detained in prison, in Serb prison, were not only -- were not political prisoners.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's leave to one side the time of war. I'm talking about the time prior to the war and throughout the last 12 years. Were there any political prisoners in the prisons themselves before the terrorists?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There were? Is that what you're saying? Do you know who they were?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Ukshin Hoti is one example. He was tried eight years ago.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. Mr. Milosevic, it's now half past ten, and we're going to adjourn for 20 minutes. How much longer do you think you're going to be with this witness?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It depends on his answers. I have questions and subquestions, Mr. May. I will probably need about one or two hours. Who knows? It all -- my questions have to do with what the witness said yesterday. So many lies. That many lies demands a lot of questions, and that is why the Court is here.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We're not -- we're not going to listen to any comments now, but we should aim, if possible, to finish this witness today. Has the amicus got any questions?

utterances.speaker: MR. WLADIMIROFF
utterances.text: No, Your Honour.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Thank you.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that Albanians were dismissed from work en masse, although you know full well that there was a directive issued by Albanian separatist parties to boycott going to work. Do you know this word, "boycott," and the concept that I just described? Is it familiar to you?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, the independent labour union of Kosova did indeed use the word "boycott" in order so that the workers of Kosova would not sign the declaration of loyalty towards the Serb state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That's another issue. But since you've just opened it up, I have to digress myself. What declaration on loyalty to the Serbian state are you talking about? Was there a declaration on loyalty to the Serbian state; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there was a declaration of loyalty towards the Serb state in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Who wrote this declaration?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The responsible organs of the Serb state in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since this is the first time that I've heard about some declaration of loyalty, could you please give us the text of this declaration? Could you provide it for us, this declaration of loyalty to the Serbian state that allegedly Albanians were required to sign?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I can bring it to Court as soon as I return to Pristina and get it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that nobody in Serbia knows or has heard of this declaration, starting from me?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I did not know that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But as I understand it, you are familiar with the word "boycott" when referring to work obligations proclaimed by the so-called Independent Trade Union of Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the trade unions were under pressure from the membership as to what to do if people would be asked -- forced to sign such a declaration.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you claim that they were required to sign a declaration in order to be able to work?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Can you provide us with one of those signed statements or declarations?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I'm sorry, I don't have it with me at the moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you make a distinction between a person who is dismissed and a person who boycotts going to work?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this specific case, there is no distinction, because Albanian workers were collectively put in an intolerable position, collectively and personally, each one, to be forced upon their knees. They were forced on their knees, and for this reason, it's the same as being thrown out of your job.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And through what means were they thrown to their knees?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: By the fact that they were being forced to show loyalty to the Serb state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since that is not true, can you perhaps tell us what document issued by the government of Serbia asked for this declaration of loyalty by Albanian residents?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't have one of these forms with me, but, Honourable Judges, I am sure I can send it from Pristina.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All right. Since we're talking about this now, since we are mentioning the power structure in Serbia, which body was responsible for issuing this declaration? Was it the government? Was it the parliament? Was it me, as the president of the Republic? Was it some ministry? So which body within the power structure, according to you, issued this phantom-like declaration that had to be signed?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I cannot answer the question concretely.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that something that is being carried out en masse, and publicly, can in fact be issued in secret and then distributed; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have no comment to your question.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you, yes or no. You are not giving an interview to the newspapers here. You are under oath.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I realise that I am before Court. I'm telling you, the accused, that I do not wish to reply.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli --

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: You have seen this document?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: And you know who issued it, where it came from?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] This document came from the directorates of the authorities which were imposed by Belgrade upon the companies in question.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... the document itself?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... question.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] The document was distributed and was imposed by the authorities forced upon Kosova companies from Serbia, by Serbia.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Continue, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So this story about the declaration is becoming a bit more clear to me. So as I understand it, you are claiming that the administrative bodies, or administrative organs of the Kosova enterprises were appointed by the authorities in Belgrade and that these organs of enterprises asked their employees to sign some declarations. Blank pages inserted to ensure pagination corresponds between the French and English transcripts. Pages 582 to 592.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And based on that, you conclude that this task was assigned to them by the government of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And this is something that you saw happen?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And an enterprise. Which enterprise?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In Trepca, the thermoelectric centre in Obilic. Those two cases I know of.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So in two enterprises you know that somebody asked Albanian employees to give this loyalty declaration?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what was this supposed to mean, this loyalty declaration? They were citizens of Serbia. What loyalty are we talking about here?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The meaning was that Albanians in Kosova, they did not feel that they were citizens of Serbia, and they declared in a referendum that they were for the Republic of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And what is stated in that declaration that they had to sign in the Trepca and Obilic enterprises?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: A free interpretation would be: I am loyal to the Serb state, to the Serb government, and to the leadership of Serbia and the leadership of the enterprise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you mean the leadership of the enterprise or the leadership of Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Leadership of the enterprise.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does that mean that the employees were supposed to give a confidence vote to the leadership of their enterprises?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. They had to give their loyalty -- or to vote on their loyalty about the Constitution, the constitutional change in Serbia, under which the autonomy of Kosova was annulled.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You are saying that the constitutional changes, in fact, abolished the autonomy of Kosova; is that what you're saying? We will get to that question later on.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. It could be called autonomy today, yesterday, or under your reign, but the contents of the autonomy, that's what you destroyed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So to my question concerning whether you made a distinction between a person who was dismissed and a person who boycotts going to work implied that there was no difference between them. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In this case.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. And you explained that you supported that with a political view, political position of those who wanted an independent Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is the political position concerning the status of some territory from the constitutional, legal point of view have anything to do with the right to employment and work that somebody has at any enterprise? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it has a connection.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that those who want Kosovo to be a republic can boycott going to work to Trepca and Obilic for legitimate reasons? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, because the enterprises were -- had been transformed into state enterprises of Serbia, and their leadership were appointed from Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The power company was -- in Serbia was always a state-owned company.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The electric company was always a big Serb company as a state organisation and -- but had no connection with other similar enterprises in Kosova such as ElektroKosova. ElektroKosova was never under -- subjected to the Serb electric company. It was only when Milosevic arrived and the changes, the constitutional changes, took place.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you know yourself that that is not true because the electrical power system is something that is of a comprehensive nature and has to be linked between its various components, so the electrical power of Kosovo could be as independent as the one in Vojvodina and other areas, and you know that the electric power system is one unit.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, from a technical point of view and from technical questions, of course. But they were completely -- the two enterprises were completely independent of one another. They had no links.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Let's leave your opinion aside. You've just explained to us that the workers in Kosovo had every reason to boycott going to work because of political reasons, because they wanted Kosovo to be an independent republic. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
