utterances.text: Which means that they boycotted going to work for political reasons, not because they were dismissed. This is the very reason I asked you whether you made a distinction between somebody who boycotted going to work and somebody who was dismissed. There is no country in this world where somebody can refuse going to work for political reasons and then claim to have been dismissed. Nowhere in the world can you see an example of this. You said so, I think. Everything is clear now. We can go on.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is clear.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that Albanians did not attend the celebrations in Gazimestan, the celebrations of the battle.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: They did not.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you sure that out of 2 million people in Gazimestan there was not a single Albanian?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I can be -- if I'm sure that there was any Albanian there, there might be one, but I know that the Albanians did boycott your speech in Gazimestan.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware that the entire Presidency of Yugoslavia, including representatives of all Yugoslav republics, were present at Gazimestan? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Exactly the opposite. None of the members of the leadership -- some of the members of the leadership, under your insistence, were there. The Slovenes arrived but not the others. There were not even diplomatic representatives there, then no Albanians. You tried to raise a mass atmosphere there for your own political purposes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, do you know that there is film footage and TV footage showing that, without exception, representatives of all republics attended the event at Gazimestan, including the Presidency of Yugoslavia? And with the exception of one or two members of the Diplomatic Corps, all members were present. Do you know this?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know that, and I don't believe it. Well, there may have been, but not the way you say it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are saying that this is not how it was. Excellent.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Based on what do you believe that none of the Albanians should have attended the celebrations in Gazimestan?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't say they ought not to attend. I said that they did not attend, the Albanians, because they felt themselves -- I understood the motives of Milosevic and why he held that big celebration. They were only nationalists. There were nationalist reasons. There were 2 million Serbs from all southern Serbia who arrived in Kosova. They knew what type of speeches would be held there, and when the -- the speeches were heard, they realised it was true.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We will get on more quickly if you keep your answers fairly short, please. Mr. Milosevic, we have, I think, exhausted this topic now.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that based on the 1974 Constitution everything was fine. This Constitution was amended in 1989; is that so?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you do know, don't you, how many demonstrations there were prior to 1989? So between 1974 until 1989 when, according to you, everything was perfect, do you know how many destructive demonstrations with the same requirement for a Kosovo republic were there? Do you know about these demonstrations?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I know about the demonstrations, but didn't say that the Constitution of 1974 was the best possible solution. The Constitution of 1974 was a compromise between the will of the Albanian people, which didn't want any -- to have anything in common with the Serb government and with Serb rule and wanted to be an independent republic and the situation, the balance of forces at the time in Yugoslavia in which -- under which it -- full autonomy had been given to them within the federation within -- but within the framework of Serbia. There were, even after the Constitution was approved and later, and in 1981 and after 1981, there were many, because the objective of the Albanians was to have that Kosova be a republic, not like -- like Croatia, like Slovenia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: These demonstrations in 1981, were they justified?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The demonstrations of 1981, in fact, expressed precisely this objective of the Albanian people who wanted to bring about such changes to ensure that Kosova became a republic. Since I was chairman of the regional committee, I say then and I say now that they were not reasonable. I did not solidarise with them. I did not solidarise, however, with the assessments made by Serbia and by Yugoslavia, namely that these demonstrations are a counter-revolution. In the communist vocabulary, it means use of violence, unlimited violence against the people. That is why I had a conflict with the party that I belonged up to that moment.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: With the constitutional changes in 1989, were the Albanians -- were any human rights or civil rights or minority rights abolished with those changes of the Constitution?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And we knew -- you know what I mean by human rights, civilian rights, minority rights. With the 1989 constitutional changes, were the Albanians stripped of any of these rights, human rights, civil rights, and minority rights?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Following the changes you made to the Constitution in 1989, some individual rights, civic rights, and national rights of Albanians have been impaired.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Which rights were abolished? It is easy to say. You have the 1974 Constitution, and you have the amendments in 1989. Now, tell us, please, which were the human, civil, and national rights that the Albanians were stripped of that had existed in the 1974 -- under the 1974 Constitution? What did the changes, the amendments abolish? Tell us, please. Enumerate just one of them, just one.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The right to organise themselves, to have their own self-governance.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: "Self [inaudible]", says the witness.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And to promote, culture, science, all the functions which they had before under the autonomy granted by the Constitution of 1974. All had been taken away. Isn't it a violation of the collective civil and human rights?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, I am asking you whether the constitutional changes took away any of the rights of the Albanians, civil rights, civic rights, human rights?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I say substantially yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You will have to compare the 1974 Constitution and the 1989 amendments and tell us: Which right was abolished by which constitutional amendment? Are you able to do that?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm trying to do that now orally. You have taken away the elementary right of self-governance, which we used to do in an autonomous way. You took away our right to have our own police. You took away our right to make our own political forecasts. You took away our right to have our own education and prepare our own curricula. But excuse me, I can later, if Your Honours are interested, I can bring you further details explaining to you where our elementary rights have been violated as citizens and as a nation, these constitutional amendments that were dictated to us by Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: I have no doubt that in due course, these documents will be put in front of us and we will be able to make our own minds up about them. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, do the Albanians have their own national state? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What is the name of that state?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Republic of Albania.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Republic of Albania, you say. Is Kosovo part of Albania?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it is not. Kosovo is not part of the -- sorry. Yugoslav. You said Serb. Sorry. It's not part of the Albanian state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Kosovo an autonomous province within Serbia?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It used to be, and that was a compromise solution reached at given moments of our history, but --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What moment of history are you talking about?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm talking about the Constitution after the Second World War, and we have always had the status of autonomy in the context of Serbia. That's a fact. But the objective, the aspiration of the Albanian people, as of 1912, has always been that this was the wrong solution for them, to have Kosova under the Serb state, and this has been always the case with the Albanian people, thinking that Kosova does not like to be under the rule of Serbia. Therefore, the Albanian people of Kosova have declared their will to set up their own independent Republic of Kosova, outside the jurisdiction and rule of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is Kosovo and Metohija -- were they an autonomous province, both according to the constitutional changes of 1989?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Formally, yes. By name, yes, but not in the content, in essence, because nothing was decided by the Kosova institutions.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you give those explanations from the aspects of an independent Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I didn't understand the question. Please repeat it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you giving us those explanations from the standpoint of an independent Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I am giving this assessment in terms of the autonomy Kosova enjoyed before you came to power and before you amended the constitutional position of Kosova. With respect to the people of Kosova, they are not in favour of your Constitution and not in favour of our Constitution of 1974. That is, they are determined to have their own Republic of Kosova, where all citizens are equal - Turks, Bosnians, Romas - to have interethnic tolerance, which at this moment does not exist, but we are going to build it, establish good relations, neighbourly relations with Serbia and its people, as well as Montenegro, Macedonia, and Albania. This is our objective, to have independent Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are now striving, in fact, for an independent Kosovo. Do you know that the conditions under which the war was stopped, and in the name of Chernomyrdin and Ahtisaari brought in, are such that they guarantee the sovereignty and territorial integrity of Yugoslavia, and that it is on the basis of conditions accepted in this way that the 1244 resolution of the United Nations Security Council was brought in, in which all this was reiterated, repeated, guaranteeing the sovereignty and territorial integrity of the Federal Republic of Yugoslavia, and that this enabled and guaranteed the protection of all the citizens of Kosovo, the population of Kosovo, and a political solution to the issue? By what you are now saying, are you yourself, therefore, against showing respect for the conditions under which the war was stopped and are against respect of the United Nations Resolution 1244, UN Security Council Resolution 1244, which sets this out and establishes that?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I said that what the objective and aspiration of the Albanian people of Kosovo is, but we all respect and abide by Resolution 1244, endorsed by the Security Council, and we think that there is still a long way to go before we will need the international administration of Kosova for quite some time, before we start the process of starting to build our democratic, political, and state institutions in Kosova, and then, from that, we can start negotiations on determining the final status of Kosova. But even when that time comes, I want to tell you what the orientation, the inclination, and determination of the Albanian people of Kosova is. This does not run counter in any way to Resolution 1244. We have never sought to make changes of the existing borders; that is, we do not want to impair in any way the territorial integrity of Yugoslavia. We want to respect it. Regarding the sovereignty of Yugoslavia and Serbia in Kosova, it is not existent for three years now, and the new reality is such that they do not have any sovereignty there.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, I think we're now moving some way from the subject matter of this trial. Mr. Milosevic, can we go on to another topic now?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, we can, but I just have to indicate the fact that this rhetoric on the alleged respect of the conditions under which the war was stopped and Resolution 1244 is in complete contradiction with the answer given previously, when asked whether he strove for an independent Kosovo. But I will move on.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said that the people of Kosovo, at a referendum, decided for a Kosovo republic, that they opted for that. What about the Serb people in Kosovo? Did they opt for a Kosovo republic as well?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, or not yet. I hope that tomorrow, sometime in the future, the Serb people of Kosova, as citizens of Kosova, will share their fate with the bulk of the Kosovars who are Albanians and will reconcile to the fact that they are no longer citizens of Serbia but are citizens of Kosova, who have full rights and are guaranteed -- their life is guaranteed in the Republic of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, I understand your need to use all this rhetoric and to utter all these things, in view of your newly established political positions, but I should like you to answer my questions with a yes or no, because they have all been put in such a way that a yes-or-no answer is possible. So what I have just asked you is whether the Serb people in Kosovo opted for a Kosovo republic.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not yet, I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Not yet, you say. What about the Turks? Did they come out in favour of a Kosovo republic, the Turks in Kosovo? Or to make it shorter, without asking you one by one, the Goranis, the Muslims, did they too opt for Kosovo republic? And whether your uni-national referendum for a Kosovo republic, a territory which is part of Serbia and where seven ethnic groups live, do you identify the Albanians with the Albanian nation, with the Albanian people, and part of the territory of a sovereign state with the status of a right to secession, whereas a moment ago you said that the Albanians have a national state of their own and that the name of that national state is the Republic of Albania? Do you therefore consider that the Albanians should have two states and the Serbs not have a single state?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just a moment, Mr. Milosevic. Mr. Milosevic, we're getting away from the original question. The original question -- just, Mr. Bakalli, listen. The original question was: Did the Turks - and one or two other nationalities were referred to - did they support the referendum or not? Did they favour a Kosovo republic or not? Perhaps you can answer that shortly.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Under the will and the election programmes of the political parties of Bosnians, Romas, Turks, they are all -- they have stated they are all for declaring Kosovo an independent republic. The Serbs, no.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Not yet.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. That is the answer. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know of a single state, a single country, in which a national minority proclaimed its own state while killing and evicting all the other inhabitants and citizens? Do you know of a single example in the world? Can you quote a single example? Let me repeat --

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm clear. I can't cite here world examples, but please, don't forget that when we are talking about Kosova, we are talking about 90 per cent of its population being Albanian, and their rights can be granted only if they have their independence from Serbia. But by establishing the Republic of Kosova, we are not saying that they are establishing the Albanian Republic of Kosova. We will establish the Republic of Kosova, composed of all the nationalities, all the ethnic groups, who have equal rights. It would be absurd to say that there are two national states. The Republic of Albania is an Albanian state, Kosova is state of Kosovars, where 90 per cent are Albanians.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Next question, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I asked for an answer to my question, and I didn't ask for a speech about Albanian separatism. What I asked was very specific. I asked: Do you know of a single country in which the national minority proclaimed its state and killed and evicted all the other citizens with the state proper agreeing to that and allowing that to happen? Do you know of any such example or not?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Albanians are not a national minority in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've taken this as far as we can. Mr. Milosevic, move on, please.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In view of the fact that a moment ago you stated that you did not agree -- you expressed your disagreement from earlier days and you failed to answer my question of why demonstrations existed from 1974 until 1989 when everything was fine, I would like to remind you of certain events, and I should like to ask you to answer some of my questions in that regard. Why were there demonstrations in 1981, for example, when the Constitution was changed 18 years later in 1989 or, rather, eight years later in 1989? Why were demonstrations held then in 1981?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think I answered this question, but I will, however, say that these demonstrations wanted the acceleration of the process for the building of Kosova outside any state links with Serbia, that is, for the republic of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You say that those demonstrations called for a development -- do you remember that you yourself were President of the Committee of National Defence and Social Self-protection at the time the demonstrations were being held in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that you personally, Mahmut Bakalli, in your capacity as President of the Committee for Total and National Defence, or All People's Defence, on the 2nd of April, at a meeting asked for the Yugoslav People's Army to bring tanks out onto the streets?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: [Indiscernible], says the witness.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: There are transcripts and reports about that, Mr. Bakalli.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: This is not at all true. When the state Yugoslav leadership -- I don't remember the date.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Your answer is no, then, is it?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. Then I said this is not right to use the army.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Both of you, one moment. Now, you may make a short explanation, Mr. Bakalli.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I have always thought that we should not dramatise demonstrations of 1981, should not involve in them the army. The Yugoslav leadership, the state, not the party, the state leadership - they were eight persons - they have decided without my presence - I was in Pristina then - to mobilise the army, the Yugoslav army in Kosova. I expressed my displeasure at that, and I felt really bad when I saw a commander, military commander, telling me that he had orders to bring the army troops in the streets, which I considered an erroneous act.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Very well. Very well. You've given -- you have given the explanation. You have given the explanation. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is not contestable that the army is led by the federal peaks of power. Therefore, it is not contested that the Presidency ordered that tanks go out onto the streets. But it is being contested -- what I asked you is being contested, that they ordered that at your request, at your demand. You called upon the JNA to bring out the tanks on that 2nd of April. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The next question. On that same day at 1700 hours, you called for the aeroplanes to be taken out as well. Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember that on the 17th of April, 1981, that is to say several days later when the situation had calmed down, you held a press conference with foreign journalists?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember, furthermore, that you told the foreign journalists, and I quote you, Mr. Bakalli, from the newspapers, you said the following: "The demonstrations, for us, were not a surprise, but the brutality of the enemy was." Do you remember having said that?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I have said -- I may have said even worse things.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What did you say?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It is possible. I may have used even harsher terms. I was not in solidarity with those demonstrations, but I was not also for them being called anti-revolutionary, counter-revolutionary.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you remember having said on the occasion, and I'm going to quote you literally again, I'm not going to recount but to quote: "The Albanian nationalists are the aiders and abettors of the occupiers against the true interests of the Albanian people"?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have nothing against that. I agree with you there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But did you say that on that occasion?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that and I say now that I have my reservations against Albanian nationalism. It is possible that I said that.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you confirm that you did.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Asked by a foreign journalist that you were not too hardcore toward the demonstrators, that you said, and I quote you again: "We're not dealing with our hardcore qualities. Their requests are not only political but are of a hostile nature in comparison with our Constitution." Correct?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You have collected all my statements in the press. I personally have forgotten those times. But it is possible, Mr. Milosevic. I was then and I am now, I think, of the opinion that the demonstrations of 1981 were not necessary. But they wanted, as I said, to have a republic for Kosova. But Constitutions cannot be amended through demonstrations staged in the streets. I think that they should be changed in the manner through normal democratic procedures which should be provided by the Constitution too.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, will you please give me a yes or no answer? I quoted your statement. Was it yours or not? Say -- I didn't collect any information, because I didn't know that you would be a witness. I do not receive any mail. I read in the newspapers that you would be a witness, and I read your denial where you say you wouldn't be a witness. So until yesterday, I didn't know whether you were actually going to be a witness or not, and I'm just taking into account what you said yesterday.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, what's the question? Mr. Bakalli, I think you were being asked about your statements in 1981, and your answer appears to be that you don't remember, but it's possible that you did say those things. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes. Yes, it is possible that I said that. But this does have nothing to do with the process of Milosevic, the trial of Milosevic. I don't see the relation.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Well, we'll be the judges of that. Yes, Mr. Milosevic, next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I agree that this has nothing to do with my trial nor is this a trial, but let me continue.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was your assessment, and I quote again at the time: "Albanian nationalism and irredentism was the basic form of enemy hostile demonstrations. The ultimate goal was clear and that was an attachment of Kosovo to Albania"? End of quotation. I agree with you once again that it was true that that was the goal, but was that your position at the time? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I doubt that I said anywhere about Kosova's annexation to Albania.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. You've answered my question. I don't expect anything from you, just to say yes or no to my questions. You said yesterday that according to the 1974 Constitution, Kosovo had the same rights as the other republics. Those were your words which I jotted down. Now, was Kosovo a republic according to that Constitution?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. In the normative part of the Constitution, it was identical to all the other republics, including the Republic of Serbia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I'm asking you, Mr. Bakalli, in view of the fact that you've said that Kosovo, by virtue of the 1974 Constitution, had the same rights as the other republics, so it is on that quotation of yours that I base my question. Was Kosovo a republic according to the 1974 Constitution? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, it was not a republic, but it enjoyed more a substantive autonomy.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you. And you claim that a -- the Autonomous Province of Kosovo was abolished in 1989 and that since 1989, the Autonomous Province of Kosovo and Metohija does not exist, no longer exists?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not according to the Constitution of 1974, perhaps with some formal name.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Thank you very much. Who exerted pressure for the exodus of the population, the Serbs or the Albanian extremists from 1981 onwards? Do you know that under pressure, up until 1988, another 40.000 Serbs left Kosovo, moved out of the Kosovo? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I have heard about this figure also in another occasion. Allow me, since this is a sensitive issue, to say that of 40.000 Serbs were given out of Kosova during 1981 -- left Kosova during 1981, 1989, you should know that they were not forced to leave out of the pressure of the Albanians, because in fact the power was being taken over gradually by the Serbs and the Serbian army forces.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, what was the total number of the Serb population in Kosovo at that time?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] At that time, let's say 8 per cent. About 8 per cent. About 150.000 to 200.000. But it is interesting to note while they have left Kosova when Serbia started to rule Kosova --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Never mind. Never mind that. I just wanted to get the total number of the Serb population at that time, and you said it was between a 150.000 to 200.000.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Yes, about 200.000.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE ROBINSON
utterances.text: Thank you. Mr. Milosevic, continue.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] That figure is incorrect but there will be plenty of time to provide the right figures.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday that you wrote articles from 1981 and that you have gone on doing so to the present day.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Not since 1981, no.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: All this time, then -- and you were critical in those articles you wrote. You were critical towards the political leadership, you say. You were critical towards me and so on and so forth. That's what you said. Now I'm asking you whether you had any repercussions or unpleasantness due to this.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Personally, no, but my friends, yes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You were asked about yourself.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: In my day, the times you're talking about, and you refer to them as "in my day," were you in any kind -- ever under any kind of house arrest? Because you mentioned --

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Previously.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I see. Previously. So you weren't, were you?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said yesterday, in the midst of giving some explanations, and then you happened to remember just a little while later that allegedly in a talk with me you told me, when the two of us had a meeting, that the police was committing crimes and that I should take care, that the balance of forces would not always be what it was then. And is it true that you threatened me on that occasion and that you used the term "crimes"? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: And I also used the phrase that there is a clergy man above every clergy man.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I heard you say that. Now, as you were speaking about apartheid, why didn't you mention apartheid to me at all when you met with me ten years ago and when you wrote about it, as you say, ten years ago?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You have asked all that, and he has answered. He said -- he said earlier, in answer to a question, that he should have done. There's no need to answer, Mr. Bakalli.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were you in active service while I was President of Serbia and Yugoslavia? Were you in any kind of active service? What do you mean "active service"?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't have any active service after 1981.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Within the frameworks of rights and the law and all standards above all European and world standards, was there an Albanian Academy of Sciences until the boycott began? Is that true? Was there an academy of sciences of Kosovo? Did it exist? An Albanian one, of course. Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The academy of science of Kosovo has existed and it exists, but it is not called the Albanian Academy of Sciences.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. It's called -- it was called the Kosovo one. Now, do you know the example -- can you quote the example of any other country in the world where national minorities had the same rights that the Albanians had? Can you quote another example in the world, of any country in the world where this existed?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about what kind of Yugoslavia you are talking about. If you are talking about your own Yugoslavia, I think that the example is quite obvious for everyone, that there couldn't be any worse position than that of the Albanians anywhere else in the world, I think. You should not forget that you have committed not only crimes against Albanians, but you wanted to evict them. How can you ask me now if there is any other country --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You're being asked about the academy, yes. Yes, Mr. Milosevic. Next question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know the violence exerted by Albanian extremists over Serbs during the time that you were in power in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Violence in Kosova, even when I was in power, existed, of course, but there was no pressure against the Serbs. If there has been some conflicts between Albanians and Serbs, under our severe laws, we have condemned them. I just want to remind you of the case of murder of an Albanian -- a case of a Serb, committed by an Albanian from Pec/Peja. He was sentenced to death and he was executed. So I mean to say that both politically and juridically, we have been very severe against any kind of pressure or any interethnic conflict. You should not forget that we used to follow a positive policy towards the Serbs of Kosova. They have had their jobs, they have been always in a higher position than the local inhabitants. Some of the Serbs have left Kosova for socioeconomic reasons. In my time, for example, 375.000 Albanians left Kosovo and went to Western Europe, to America, New Zealand, Australia, because --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, that is enough in answer to the question.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, as I see your reply to my question whether you knew about the violence of Albanian extremists against Serbs during the time you held power in Kosovo, the answer was yes.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was no violence, at least not in the sense that you are trying to imply.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that after 1980 --

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: After 1981 -- in the army, for instance, someone had killed a Serb in the army, and our judges, according to the laws, in accordance with the laws, sentenced him to execution, to death, and he was executed, according to law. I can't swear that the Albanians are angels and they don't know how to commit crimes. I'm not saying that. But in the essence, the Albanians were the subjects, and our organs were mobilised so that there would be no conflict between the Serbs and other nationalities.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Among Serbs and other nationalities, there were no conflicts at all, Mr. Bakalli.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The translation was incorrect. I meant between Albanians and Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, since you're mentioning Serbs and other nationalities, you should probably know that there are 27 ethnic groups living in Serbia. The legal, social, and civic status of the Albanian ethnic group, as far as the state is concerned, the legal system, and everything else that constitutes the status of an ethnic group -- therefore, is the status of Albanians in any way different from the status of Hungarians, Slovaks, Bulgarians, and so on? I don't want to enumerate all of the ethnic groups. Is there anything that creates a distinction as far as the legal and constitutional framework, as far as the human and civic framework is concerned, within the whole system? Is there any difference in the status of these ethnic groups; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For instance -- yes. Serb nationalism, for the Serb nationalists, the Albanians were simply in the way. There are 2 million Albanians at the moment. You can't compare that to an occupation of, say, 20.000 Bulgarians, 30.000 Romanians, and others. There are 2 million Albanians living on their own land.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, do you know that 70.000 Albanians live in Belgrade? Do you know of any case of discrimination against an Albanian? Furthermore, along the Boulevard of Revolution, which you walked many times probably, one can see numerous shops with the names of their Albanian owners. Was a window of any shop ever broken? Do you know of any case of violence against the 70.000 Albanians living in Belgrade; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, there were cases, both in Belgrade and in Serbia. The attitude with respect to Albanians living there is something that you simply do not wish to remember.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Yes. I'd like to see some examples of that. Are you aware of murders and rapes and destruction of homes and arson of homes, fields, and so on? So all of these means were used by Albanian nationalists to expel Serbs, and under their pressure, that I've mentioned, 40.000 Serbs had to leave Kosovo. Do you know anything of this?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that that's exaggerated for Serb propaganda, and I don't accept it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So dead people constitute Serb propaganda as well?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For the dead --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, there is no need to answer. We'll hear further evidence in due course. Anything else, Mr. Milosevic?

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Certainly.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, how many newspapers in Albanian were published in the province up until the war, the 24th of March, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It depends on the period. Sometimes Rilindja was issued, and then it was forbidden by the Serb government. And then Bujku was issued, and then the Serb authorities had illegalised Bujku. And then another newspaper which was issued and then banned. And then Koha Ditore, which was subject to various types of pressure. And then Zeri was issued, and then Zeri Javore, Zeri Ditore. So what I mean is the medias did exist in Kosova. At this moment, there are a lot of media, but under Milosevic at the time, they were born and then they were killed. They were born and then banned, born and banned. Various types of pressures. That you know very well.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It is my assertion, Mr. Bakalli, that none of the Albanian newspapers in Kosovo were banned. Is that true or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Even foreign diplomats, including Americans, used to tell me, Mr. Bakalli, that they were able to buy all Albanian press, all Albanian Kosovo press, at every corner, and now you're claiming that there was no freedom of press for Albanians in Kosovo.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You were talking about freedom of the press. You asked: Were they issued? I said: Yes, they were issued and then banned, issued and banned, issued and banned. And the Americans, or the American you're talking about certainly did see newspapers. But the history of journalism in Kosova in the past would be quite a surprising history of births and of banning of various newspapers. That's a question of the government. It's not a financial problem.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, I'm not discussing internal problems of a newspaper. What I'm referring to is that none of the newspapers were banned. You are claiming that that's not true.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's not true.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You've mentioned Koha Ditore just a while ago. Have you read the Rambouillet agreement which was published by Koha Ditore in its entirety in the Albanian language? Yes or no, please.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that I read all the documents -- I heard about all the documents in Rambouillet. But remember, at the time I was in Switzerland and was working on a project, a Swiss/Kosova project at the time, and I don't remember the exact text of Koha Ditore, but I do know the essence of the proposals of the Rambouillet documents, which you did not sign because that was not to your advantage to enter into negotiations. You didn't want to lose the opportunity to rule over Kosova.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just try and stick to the point, Mr. Bakalli, and we'll all get on more quickly. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Since you are saying that you worked on this Swiss project, as a result of which you were not in Pristina, do you know that the entire Rambouillet document was published in two parts by the Koha Ditore newspaper?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know it, but I believe you that it was published, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know about this?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know it, but I do believe you that it was published, yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that it was published even before the meeting in Rambouillet started?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I'm sorry, I don't really know. I wasn't in Kosova at the time.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you don't know about it. Do you know how many Albanians were killed by Albanian terrorists in 1998 and beginning of 1999? Do you know how many Albanians were killed by Albanian terrorists?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I do not know. When you use the word "terrorism," if you're talking about the KLA, I could tell you that they did not commit any criminal murders. If they did commit any criminal murders, they should be taken to court and tried, like every citizen of Kosova. No one is above the law or outside the law, the competence of the law. But I don't know of any number. If you have arguments, okay, bring them to trial, in national trials, in the national courts of Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think that when somebody plants a bomb at the market, as a result of which a lot of people are killed, do you believe that to be an act of terrorism? Or do you believe when somebody opens fire at the cafe full of young people, that constitutes an act of terrorism?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you think that it's an act of terrorism when somebody intercepts a forest keeper who is an Albanian and kills him? Do you believe that to be an act of terrorism?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It's a crime. Murder is a crime and you have to be taken to court.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: But you don't believe this to be an act of terrorism. Is it an act of terrorism when --

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Throwing a bomb is --

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it an act of terrorism when somebody comes to the door of a house of an Albanian physician, who is a good doctor and is employed at a state hospital as a decent man, and somebody comes and kills him at the doorstep of his own house? Isn't that an act of terrorism?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The KLA did not do that. I know that. And if someone did commit such crimes, it was an individual initiative. Excuse me, Your Honours. I did express my reserves about the declarations of the Ministry of Justice of Serbia, who, in the last -- over the last few months declared again and again that we should be sending people to The Hague. If you want people, then you have to look among the members of the KLA and see.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, we will not get on if we have these very long answers. It would be much better if you would just restrict yourself to the questions. We'll adjourn now for 20 minutes.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We'll go on with the evidence until half past one. At half past one we've got to stop to deal with some procedural matters. Mr. Milosevic, if you can -- if you would get through your cross-examination by then, we'd be grateful.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I shall try to do so.

utterances.speaker: THE INTERPRETER
utterances.text: Microphone for Mr. Milosevic, please.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Microphone. Your microphone.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It turned off by itself.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Therefore, when I asked you whether you knew how many Albanians were killed by Albanian terrorists in 1998 and 1999, and they killed and kidnapped hundreds of them, the way I understand your answer is that you didn't know about this. Did I understand you well?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I didn't know about that well. I know about a crime that was committed in 1988 to 1989 about a -- against a Serb in Kosova by someone of the Albanian side, by one of the KLA, of the UCK.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You used the phrase "if somebody had committed a crime" then this is how it was. Since you are saying "if somebody had committed a crime," I take it that you don't know whether somebody in fact did. My question pertained to Albanian policemen, forest keepers, physicians, mailmen, and so on. But let me get on with another question. Do you know how many Albanians served in the police force of the Ministry of the Interior of Kosovo and Metohija during those same years, 1998 and 1999?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Could you please repeat the question about the police force?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many Albanians served in the police force in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In my time or do you mean in 1998, 1999?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I mean in recent years, 1998, 1999?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, you eliminated all the Albanians on the police force in Kosova when you reigned over Kosova. You eliminated them all, and they formed their own trade union. And then you said they had been organising a trade union for obstructive reasons, to -- and put a lot of policemen in prison from Kosova. So I could say that there were no or very few Albanian policemen in the years 1988, 1989 -- rather, 1998, 1999.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you are telling us that there were no police -- no Albanian policemen except for a few exceptions; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: True.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that during the summer and fall of 1988, in addition to these regular police forces -- this is a new question, therefore. So do you know that by the summer and fall of 1988, in the hundreds of Albanian villages, a local police was established? Have you heard of local police in Albanian villages?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You have not. Have you heard that in Albanian villages local policemen were elected by the village residents among themselves and that the state provided uniforms, weapons for them in order to maintain law and order in those villages? You don't know about this?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that many Serb citizens were given uniforms and were in Serb paramilitary units. That I know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When I asked you whether you knew of policemen who were local Albanian residents, you basically told me that you don't know of this. Is that right?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's true. I don't really know anything about it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know that a number of these local policemen, who were Albanians and were elected by the villagers themselves and who maintained law and order in villages, were killed by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know anything about this fact. Sincerely, I really don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Just a minute ago, you told us that there were Serb paramilitary forces there. Do you know that there was an order that applied to all units of army and police which said that in their zone of responsibility, they should arrest and disarm any paramilitary group?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. I don't know anything about a disarmament order, but I do know that a lot of crimes were committed against the Albanian people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were a lot of crimes committed by Albanians against Albanian residents?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I wouldn't think so, but if there were any cases, evidence could be brought and people could be brought to trial.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Were a lot of crimes committed by NATO against the Albanian population?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. There was collateral damage which did take place. There was one case I know of. But NATO did make a declaration, a public declaration. But in essence, the people of Kosova were not afraid at all of the NATO bombing and wasn't afraid of the members of the KLA either, because the people were deported by force, by police, paramilitary, and army, to Albania and to Macedonia.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that when NATO bombs hundreds of Albanian refugees in a convoy - and I have shown here photographs of carbonised corpses, children, and so on - you in fact are referring to this as collateral damage; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know that there was no bombing, NATO bombing, or it was not the purpose of NATO bombing to hinder -- to do anything against the civil population. It was against the system.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When a maternity home is being bombed, is that a demonstration to do no harm to the civilian population?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: That, Mr. Milosevic, is a matter of comment. It's not a -- it's not a question.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] All right, then.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how the provisional Executive Council of Kosova and Metohija in 1989 was composed?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It was appointed by the Serbian Assembly. I don't remember that, but you should know that it was appointed by the Serb Assembly; second, the majority of the members were Serbs; and third, there were also some Albanians and some Gorani, or some other nationality, whom you have taken over to your side. That was a Serb government and not a government of the Kosova people.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: When you say "Kosovo people," you in fact mean only Albanians; right?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No. No. I mean the Albanians of Kosova -- Kosovar, sorry. It was appointed by the Serb government. It was not appointed by the Kosovar Albanians or by others in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It wasn't the government; it was the assembly.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. The assembly, Serbian one.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And you believe that Kosovo, in fact, is not Serbia?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: We've been -- you need not answer that. We've been through this argument.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. Do you know that this provisional Executive Council was composed of Serbs, Albanians, Turks, Muslim, Gorani, Romany, and so on, which means all of the ethnic groups that live in Kosovo? Do you know about this?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do, but I also know that it was a tool, a blind tool, in the hands of the Serb parliament and government to rule over Kosova, and there have been some members in it of the nationalities that you mentioned, but Serbs were in greatest number, and they acted under the orders of the Serb parliament.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that in that temporary government of Kosovo, Serbs were a minority as compared to the others?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't remember, and I don't think so.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Well, there are people that I can name to you. For example, Albanian Dzafer Djukiu, who was a minister for social affairs, his throat was slashed in Pec, shortly after the UN came to Kosovo, and a bomb was planted in the house of the police minister in order to expel him from Kosovo. However, they managed to survive. My question was: Are you aware of the fact that Serbs constituted a minority in that Executive Council; yes or no?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The witness has answered that. He says he doesn't remember and he doesn't think so.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Are you aware of the fact that in the Serbian delegation in Rambouillet there were representatives from all ethnic groups from Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, formally they were, but in fact, they all were people who did not represent the will of the Kosovars. They were instruments in the hands of the Serb-Milosevic government and power, and as such they were elected.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And who did the national delegation from Kosovo represent?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The delegation of Kosova was composed of the main political parties, legal parties of Kosova, plus the representatives of the KLA.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know Hasim Thaci?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, I do.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know his nickname?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. No.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that his nickname is "Viper," "Snake"?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know of any pseudonyms.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You don't know that he got the nickname because he poisoned his political adversaries?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't think that he might have done that, and I don't know.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was it logical for you that the head of the Albanian delegation in Rambouillet be Thaci rather than Rugova? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: It was logical you say?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, logical. Yes. At that moment, the real political forces should have come together and be prepared for dialogue and agreements with Yugoslavia and with the international community. The reality, the reality that was created was such that the KLA had a dominant position. You might ask why it was so, because Mr. Milosevic did not agree to hold political negotiations in due course, and it was a forced solution under the new circumstances in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I don't wish to go back to those 11 times the delegation of the Serbian government went to Kosovo, but let me ask you this: Do you know how many Rugova associates, political activists of his party were killed by Thaci's terrorists?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: No, I don't. I haven't followed these developments. I know that some murders have been committed in Kosova which in fact have not yet been elucidated, and we will do that in due course. We see who is behind them.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you consider those killings to be political killings, to have been political killings because they were political personages that were involved?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: For most of these murders there are statements issued by the respective political parties and UNMIK police that they cannot conclude that they were politically motivated murders. UNMIK.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So when Rugova's president of the municipal board of his party dies in a particular place, loses his life, that is not in a political killing?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: It may; it may not. We have not to prejudice, a priori pass judgement on any murder that has been committed before evidence is presented and ruling is made.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know how many Serbs, Montenegrins, Muslims, Croats, Goranis, Romanies, Egyptians and other non-Albanian inhabitants were expelled from Kosovo and Metohija after the arrival of KFOR by the Albanian extremists?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You mentioned the word -- where our state. I may say that unfortunately the number of national minorities who -- especially of Serbs was very great who, after the KFOR forces arrival, left Kosova, intimidated or afraid that some acts of revenge might be taken against them, fearing the consequences of the tragic situation which was created in Kosova then. The political parties, Albanian political parties, and I believe the future parliament and government and UNMIK, have a plan in place to ensure their organised return in Kosova to their own lands and homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What lands and homes of their own are you talking about when the terrorists, after the arrival of KFOR set fire to several tens of thousands of Serb houses and homes? Are you aware of that?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: If there are such cases, then we will work to assist them to build their new homes which have been ruined.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Is it possible that when we're talking about tens of thousands of houses you use the term "if," "if" that is possible, do you really have no knowledge or know nothing about what is going on in Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think you are interpreting me wrong. I said that, unfortunately, their people have left, Serbs, and other nationalities have left Kosova after the war. I didn't say if they have left Kosova. And I am certain that we will help them to return, because they, too, will become citizens of Kosova, equal to Albanian citizens, and will have assure life. We need some transitory period to do that probably.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So you believe, and please give me a yes or no answer.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Because Mr. May, you have been cautioning me that I'm hurrying, but the answers took up too much time. They could be yes or no answers, but I'm not in a position to control them, you are.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: And my question: Do you believe that KFOR could not have protected the Serbs and other non-Albanian inhabitants that were expelled from Kosovo?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I said that most of them have left Kosova not under direct pressure but out of fear that prevailed as a result of the war. And as far as I know, the KFOR and the international police are actively helping or are playing the role of security in Kosova for the Serbs that live there.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you happen to know that of 2.500 kidnapped Serbs, the fate of 1.300 is not known and that on such a small territory as Kosovo that you cannot establish that along with the presence of such a large force there? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't know about the exact figure of people who have lost, disappeared, or who were kidnapped, Serbs, but I know that there is some figure and that it should be clarified, just as the question of 3.800 Albanians who have disappeared, whom nobody knows, should be clarified.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: [Previous translation continues] ... point. Yes, Mr. Milosevic.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you consider that the fear was unjustified for people fleeing from Kosovo when you have a figure of 3.000 killed since the arrival of KFOR? Do you think the fear is unjustified?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that after the war, people are afraid and people move from their homes.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: The reasons, therefore, are not linked to the burning of tens of thousands of homes and the killing of thousands of people and the abduction of thousands of people but just some kind of abstract fear. Is that what you're saying? Is that your assessment? Yes or no?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are drawing your conclusions very quickly. I think fear was a dominant factor, but it is possible that in concrete cases, families have been evicted after the houses were burned. We will investigate these issues and take the adequate legal measures.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I quoted yesterday, not here but when I was given the floor, a speech by one of your leaders when he said, "We ensure that Kosovo will be only for the Albanians. We will secure Kosovo only for the Albanians." That was a quotation. It was published and broadcast over the radio and television. What do you think about statements of this kind made by this particular leader that "We will secure Kosovo solely for the Albanians"? Do you support that? Do you support this kind of statement?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I don't support such statements, such a logic, and I think that there can be no one, not a wise man, politically or otherwise, that can say such a thing.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: That means that there are many Albanian leaders and Albanians themselves who do not support a statement of this kind.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes. I think that most of or all of them do not support such kind of statements, because we are building Kosova for the Kosovars and not only for the Albanians alone.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Why do you keep making facial expressions, grimaces, as if you're not understanding the translation, when you studied in Belgrade and you understand every word I'm saying very well? Why do you keep making those grimaces?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: You do not need to answer that. I've had a note from the interpreters asking you both to wait until they've finished before you speak. Mr. Milosevic, we will have to, in due course, make a decision, if it's relevant, about the matters that you're raising, but it seems you've dealt very thoroughly with these particular issues. And of course, we'll be able to hear any evidence which you put before us on this particular topic. But I think we've now exhausted it, and perhaps you could move on.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] Very well.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Rugova [sic], do you know when Greater Albania existed?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You should ask Rugova. Are you asking me or Mr. Rugova?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I apologise. I meant to say you, Mr. Bakalli.

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Can you repeat the question, please, to me, address it to me again?

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know when Greater Albania existed, was in existence?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As far as I know, it has never existed, Greater Albania as such, neither today as a notion -- maybe the notion of Greater Albania exists in some political platforms of Albania in the Balkans, but neither in Tirana, nor in Tetova, Pristina. The notion of Greater Albania is a by-product of Serb political propaganda aiming at presenting the Albanians as people who struck fear among others.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, the question was: Do you know when Greater Albania existed? You say it did not exist. You don't have to go into an explanation as to why. But do you know who established a Greater Albania? Or rather, do you know that during World War II, Mussolini and Hitler established Greater Albania, and which parts of Kosovo at that time and which parts of Macedonia were included into this Greater Albania? These were historical facts, and you were a professor. Do you know about that historical fact?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I know very well, but it is considered a fascist and Nazi concoction about Albania, and not Greater Albania. The Albanians themselves, in Albania, Macedonia, and Kosova, with their anti-fascist war, by fighting against fascism and racism, Italian and German one, by taking an active part in the Second World War on the side of the alliance and as fighting as partisans, in fact, they have said that this is a fascist and Nazi concoction. So don't blame me and Albanians for that fascist creation, because we fought ourselves against it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I am not ascertaining guilt. All I am asking you is whether you have heard of that creation. You first said that you did not hear of it and now you say that it was a Nazi, fascist creation. So we've cleared that point up. Is there a project for a Greater Albania present in Kosovo today?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: In all the political parties of Kosova, Albanian political parties in Kosova, in Albania and in Macedonia, there is not any such project for the creation of some "Greater Albania," in inverted commas, but there is a project for freedom, peace, democracy, prosperity, and European integration, and the project for Kosova to become an independent state.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Very well. You therefore claim that in Kosovo, there is no political force supporting the project for a Greater Albania?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That's right.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Do you know about the terrorist attacks on the population and facilities in the south of Serbia by the KLA, effected by the KLA?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: The KLA was the National Liberation Army of Medvegje, Presheva, Bujanovc, and it is not the doing of Kosova Liberation Army, KLA. Why it happened in Presevo, these conflicts, Mr. Milosevic knows that better than I do, because they occurred within -- in the southern part of Serbia. And then after the engagement of the international community, the issue was resolved, and I think things are moving in the right direction for a peaceful solution.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Bakalli, do you know yourself anything about them?

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] You mean about Presheva?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes. That was the question. If you don't know, just say so.

utterances.speaker: THE WITNESS
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I know, but this is not -- has got nothing to do with Greater Albania. It has to do with the position of Albanians living there in Presheva.

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: The only issue here is whether you know anything about it yourself. And if you don't know, just say so and we can go on to something else.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] May we continue?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Yes.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Was the KLA disarmed upon the arrival of KFOR?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Yes, it was.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: What are they firing from, then?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You know that there is -- the arms can be sold and bought. This can happen in Serbia, in Macedonia, anywhere. So these are individual questions of arms possession. But the KLA no longer is armed.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Except individually?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: Individuals can possess arms, because in Kosovo now, we are carrying out an action for people to surrender their arms, even on an individual basis.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Does the KLA shoot in the south of Serbia and Macedonia? Is it shooting there?

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Mr. Milosevic, I'm going to stop you for one minute, because what I want you to explain is what the relevance is of what is happening today to the indictment with which we're concerned, the period of which is 1999. Now, I understand your argument about the KLA prior to that. And what is the relevance of what's happening now to this indictment? We're now dealing with events almost three years ago.

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] It can be relevant because, as I have maintained here over the past few days, that it is a protracted crime that we are dealing with, that the occupation forces in Kosovo and Metohija are doing together with the terrorist organisation of Kosovar Albanians, the KLA. This protracted crime, which was a pooling of crimes, an association and joinder of crimes - and I gave an explanation of this with respect to political, strategic, and historical reasons and conditions - is continuing, and that is why it is relevant and linked to what we're talking about

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Furthermore, do you consider, Mr. Bakalli, that it is safe and secure in Kosovo and Metohija?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: According to the estimates of UNMIK institutions, which are responsible for security in Kosovo at this moment, together with part of local police, I think that the situation in Kosovo is relatively calm and stable. I personally am not pleased with the current situation, because I think that we should do away with any manifestation of lack of -- of intolerance towards other nations and towards Serbs in particular, for which I think we need some more time. But generally speaking, the situation is, according to their estimation, safe and stable, as I said.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: You said a moment ago, half an hour ago, in fact, that no institutions have yet been built up, and that is why I asked you the question of whether you consider it to be safe and secure, because I didn't seem to feel that it was logical for it to be secure if no institutions had been built, according to what you yourself said. But you say that the situation is safe. Now, I ask you: Are you safe yourself, personally?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: As you might well know, never in my life have I been escorted by some bodyguard or police. I have always felt, when I was a leader and today, safe, in that Kosova, as it is. Nothing has happened to me. I have never been threatened, never assaulted. But there are other people who complain of being threatened and assaulted. The institution that you are referring to, this has got to do with the parliament, the government. They don't have much to do with the government -- with the security, because, as I said, this is the duty, the task of the international forces, the KFOR, and the international police of UNMIK, together with some local police. The institutions are there, the institution of security.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: So for you personally it's safe, but you're not sure it's safe for others; is that right?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: I think that everybody feels secure in Kosova.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: Except for the Serbs?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: That is not true. I am in contact with the Serbs of Kosova, and the situation is not as tragic as you are trying to take it out here. It is not as good either. We are working to overcome it.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: As 360.000 have been expelled, then there are less of them now who seem to be a problem. You said that during Rambouillet, you were in Switzerland, and prior to Rambouillet. What were you doing in Switzerland?

utterances.speaker: MAHMUT BAKALLI [Resumed]
utterances.text: You are changing your questions. I said I was there at the invitation of two Swiss institutions, for a project of theirs to build and to deal with -- to deal with the emergency situation in Kosova. I worked for that project. You are exaggerating the figures, I think. You are saying 360.000 Serbs.

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: No. I did not say --

utterances.speaker: JUDGE MAY
utterances.text: Just one moment. If you could deal with the matters shortly, Mr. Bakalli, we'll all get on. Now, is there any more questions about Rambouillet?

utterances.speaker: THE ACCUSED
utterances.text: [Interpretation] I will skip the others.

utterances.speaker: MR. MILOSEVIC
utterances.text: [Interpretation]

utterances.speaker: UNKNOWN EXAMINER
utterances.text: I have to correct you. I didn't say 360.000 Serbs. I said 360.000 inhabitants of Kosovo, mostly Serbs, but Croats, Muslims, Goranis, Egyptians, Romany, and everyone else.
